speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your follow-up. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy results not included in provided data; please refer to ENT Examination findings for postauricular tenderness and Audiology Report for hearing outcomes.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Granuloma (Surgically Induced) secondary to Tympanoplasty.

The connection between your eating-induced shooting pain and the discomfort from earrings suggests a mass or granuloma at the tympanomeatal junction, which is a known complication of ear surgery. This mass can erode the outer rim of the eardrum (causing pain with earrings) and irritate adjacent nerves, leading to referred pain during chewing.
